title: Entropy Forge — an information-theory lab (compression + error-correction)
description: An interactive information-theory and data-compression laboratory, built from scratch with zero dependencies. It measures Shannon entropy (order-0/1/2) and the theoretical compression floor, then implements and visualises every major lossless codec family — a Huffman coder with a live code-tree and canonical length table; a genuine Witten–Neal–Cleary integer arithmetic coder (32-bit registers, E1/E2/E3 renormalisation, pending-bit underflow) with adaptive order-0 and order-1 models that hug the entropy bound; LZ77/LZSS sliding-window matching with a colour-coded parse map; LZW with a self-building dictionary and variable-width codes (KwKwK handled); and a full bzip2-style Burrows–Wheeler pipeline (suffix-sorted BWT with LF-mapping inverse, move-to-front, run-length, arithmetic). Composite codecs assemble the real formats — DEFLATE-lite (LZ77 tokens entropy-coded) and bzip-lite. And now THE ACTUAL FORMAT: a from-scratch, RFC 1951-compliant DEFLATE codec — the algorithm inside gzip, zlib, PNG and ZIP — with a 32 KB hash-chain + lazy-matching LZ77 stage, all three block types (stored, the canned fixed Huffman code, and a dynamic Huffman code built by the lab's own package-merge and capped at 15 bits, its length tables run-length-compressed by the 19-symbol code-length alphabet), an auto-selector that emits the cheapest block, and a puff-style inflater. It gets DEFLATE's tricky bit order exactly right (fields pack LSB-first, Huffman codes MSB-first), wraps the payload in byte-exact gzip (RFC 1952) and zlib (RFC 1950) containers with from-scratch CRC-32 and Adler-32, and — the real proof — INTEROPERATES: the .gz it emits decompresses with the browser's own gunzip, the browser's gzip inflates here, and its auto encoder matches or beats zlib level 9 on the structured corpora. A dedicated DEFLATE & gzip page shows a live native-interop badge, a stored-vs-fixed-vs-dynamic block showdown, the 32 KB LZ parse map, the full dynamic-block anatomy (HLIT/HDIST/HCLEN + the live literal/length, distance and code-length code tables), and an annotated gzip container hex dump. It also implements tANS / FSE — the multiply-free, table-driven Finite State Entropy coder inside Zstandard and Apple's LZFSE — sharing rANS's normalised model but coding by a finite-state machine of lookups and shifts alone, cross-verified to land within a few bytes of rANS on every input. At the far frontier it now implements CONTEXT MIXING — the PAQ/lpaq family that underpins the strongest general-purpose compressors ever measured: a bit-level predictor that runs a panel of models (order-0..6 byte contexts, a word model, and a longest-match model), each keeping an adaptive per-context probability, and blends their opinions in the log-odds domain with a context-selected LOGISTIC MIXER trained by online logistic regression, then refines the blend through two SSE (secondary-symbol-estimation) adaptive-probability-map stages before a carryless 32-bit BINARY arithmetic coder spends −log₂p bits per bit — with nothing transmitted but the stream, since the decoder rebuilds the identical panel and replays every update. Across the corpus it is the strongest all-rounder, winning most inputs outright and coming within a byte or two of PPM on the rest. Its own lab page shows a live bits-per-byte learning curve, the mixer's signed per-model trust weights, per-model accuracy, a bit-by-bit prediction ribbon, and the match length climbing over repetitive data. And it now implements LZMA — the algorithm inside 7-Zip and xz, and the moment the lab's two halves finally join: instead of Huffman-coding an LZ token stream, LZMA feeds EVERY decision (is-this-a-match, is-it-a-repeat, the length, the distance slot, the literal byte) into a single from-scratch adaptive BINARY RANGE CODER whose 11-bit probabilities are chosen by a rich context — a 12-STATE machine remembering whether recent packets were literals or matches, the low position bits, the previous byte, and, on the literal right after a match, the byte that would have been copied (matched-literal coding). The four most-recent match distances live in an MRU list (rep0..rep3) recoded with a handful of context bits instead of the full distance machinery — the reason LZMA crushes data that revisits offsets — while new distances code a 6-bit magnitude slot plus a reverse-tree of near bits or direct + 4-bit align bits, and match lengths (2..273) take a low/mid/high split; an HC4 match finder (hash2/hash3 heads + a hash4 chain) with a lazy, rep-preferring parse feeds it. The encoder AUTO-TUNES its literal/position model — it races six (lc, lp, pb) presets and ships the smallest, storing the choice in the one-byte LZMA properties (the exact byte .xz records, so the stream is self-describing), which shrinks every corpus for a single transmitted byte. Its lab page lays the coder bare — a size race against every other from-scratch codec, the packet stream coloured by literal/new-match/rep0..3 with width proportional to output bytes, the distance-source breakdown that makes the rep list's payoff visible, and the live 12-state transition table. On the benchmark it is the strongest DICTIONARY coder, winning the repetitive corpus outright and leading gzip/DEFLATE/bzip on the structured ones. And now THE CAPSTONE — a from-scratch, spec-compliant PNG codec (ISO/IEC 15948, RFC 2083) with an interactive IMAGE STUDIO, the format that finally assembles the lab's own DEFLATE, zlib wrapper and CRC-32 into a real, viewable file. It supports every colour type × bit depth the spec allows (grayscale 1–16-bit, truecolour RGB/RGBA 8/16-bit, indexed palette 1–8-bit with tRNS transparency, grayscale+alpha), all five §6 scanline filters (None/Sub/Up/Average/Paeth) with a libpng minimum-sum-of-absolute-differences adaptive per-scanline chooser, Adam7 interlacing, multi-IDAT decoding and CRC-validated chunk parsing (IHDR/PLTE/tRNS/IDAT/IEND plus ancillary gAMA/pHYs/sRGB/tEXt read-out) — the whole codec round-tripping at the raw-raster level bit-for-bit across every colour type × depth × filter × interlace. PNG's one genuinely new idea, the modelling PRE-FILTER, makes the lab's through-line literal: each filter is a predictor that replaces a pixel with the small residual left after guessing it from its neighbours, measurably LOWERING the order-0 entropy of the byte stream before DEFLATE ever runs (a smooth gradient drops 6.5 → 1.0 bits/byte). The Image Studio encodes a procedural or uploaded image, drags a filter-strategy picker while a per-scanline strip shows the adaptive choices, charts total PNG size under each filter, renders the decoded pixels on a canvas, lists the byte-exact chunk table, and — the showstopper, mirroring the gzip interop proof — verifies its output against the BROWSER'S OWN native PNG decoder pixel-for-pixel (premultiplied-alpha aware), decoding the browser's PNG in turn. It is proven headlessly too: known-answer decodes of real PNGs produced by an INDEPENDENT encoder (Node's own zlib), their pixels hashed from the source pattern before our code touches them. A Benchmark page races all codecs — real gzip, tANS, context mixing and LZMA included — on eight corpora against the entropy floor, every result verified by a full decode; a live Self-test round-trips every codec across the corpus plus adversarial edge cases (empty, single-symbol, all-256-bytes, long runs, pseudo-random) — 643 in-browser checks (including a from-scratch PNG group — exhaustive raster round-trips across every colour type × bit depth × filter × interlace, and known-answer decodes of real Node-zlib PNGs) plus 28 native-gzip cross-checks — and offline fuzzes of thousands of cases (validated directly against Node's zlib, a 400-case context-mixing fuzz, and a 3,000-case LZMA fuzz across five structure classes) found zero mismatches. And now THE OTHER HALF OF SHANNON — a from-scratch CHANNEL-CODING pillar, the dual of everything above: source coding removes redundancy to hit the entropy floor, channel coding adds structured redundancy back so a message survives a NOISY CHANNEL and reconstructs EXACTLY. It builds the algebraic substrate (GF(2) linear algebra with mod-2 Gauss–Jordan/null-space, and GF(256) finite-field arithmetic with exp/log tables over primitive polynomial 0x11D), the channel models and their Shannon capacities (Binary Symmetric C=1−H(p), Binary Erasure C=1−ε, and a BI-AWGN model with log-likelihood ratios), and four families of real error-correcting codes on top. HAMMING(7,4) and the extended SEC-DED (8,4) code — syndrome decoding where the failed parity checks, read as a binary number, spell out the flipped bit's position, shown as the classic three-circle Venn picture, correcting every single error and detecting every double. REED–SOLOMON over GF(256) — the code inside QR codes, CDs, DVDs, DVB and Voyager — systematic generator-polynomial encoding and a full syndromes → BERLEKAMP–MASSEY → CHIEN search → FORNEY decoder handling both errors AND erasures via the errata locator, correcting t byte-errors or 2t erasures or any mix, and shrugging off long BURST errors that would swamp a bit-level code (validated on 7,000+ randomized trials across QR/CCSDS configs). CONVOLUTIONAL codes with the VITERBI maximum-likelihood decoder — the (7,5) K=3 and industry (171,133) K=7 'Voyager/GSM/Wi-Fi' codes — the trellis drawn out with the survivor path traced back through add-compare-select path metrics, in both hard-decision (Hamming metric) and soft-decision (Euclidean/AWGN) flavours, with a BER waterfall showing the ~2 dB soft-decision coding gain. And LDPC codes with sum-product BELIEF PROPAGATION in the log-likelihood domain — a sparse systematic parity-check code decoded on its TANNER GRAPH by variable↔check message passing iterated to convergence, the capacity-approaching family inside 5G, Wi-Fi 6 and DVB-S2, with a live scrubbable convergence and a BER waterfall. And now POLAR CODES — the first codes PROVEN to REACH the Shannon limit (Arıkan 2009) and, with LDPC, one of the two codes standardised for 5G-NR (LDPC carries the data channel, polar the control channel). Built from scratch: the CHANNEL POLARISATION transform Gₙ = F⊗ⁿ realised as an in-place, FFT-shaped butterfly (O(N log N), no matrix); two constructions that rank and freeze the synthetic bit-channels — the exact Bhattacharyya recursion for the BEC (where capacity is exactly 1−Z) and the Gaussian-approximation density evolution (Chung–Richardson–Urbanke φ/φ⁻¹) for the BI-AWGN; a recursive SUCCESSIVE-CANCELLATION decoder (min-sum f/g with partial sums stitched back up the butterfly); an SC-LIST decoder (L forking paths pruned by the exact log-domain path metric, with per-path LLR/partial-sum stacks); and CRC-AIDED SCL — the actual 5G decoder — on a from-scratch bitwise CRC that lets the list pick the survivor that checks out. Its lab page shows the polarisation staircase sharpening toward a step at capacity as N grows, the (8,4) encoder butterfly with its info/frozen inputs, a live encode → BI-AWGN → decode pipeline racing SC vs SCL vs CA-SCL with a flipped-bit strip, and a block-error waterfall where the list buys ~½ dB and the CRC steepens the cliff — exactly why 5G chose CA-SCL. The capstone Channel Lab runs BOTH theorems end to end: it gzips a message (source coding), wraps the compressed bytes in Reed–Solomon(255,223) parity (channel coding), fires it through a bursty channel, RS-repairs the damage and gunzips back byte-for-byte — while the same noise on the UNPROTECTED gzip destroys it — the separation theorem made runnable. Every code is wired into the Self-test page (679 in-browser checks including 36 channel-coding proofs: exhaustive Hamming single-error correction and SEC-DED double-error detection, GF(256) field axioms, thousands of Reed–Solomon error/burst/erasure/mixed trials, convolutional clean/single-error/soft-decision decoding with verified free distances, LDPC validity + BP correction, and — new — polar transform = Gₙ, SC/SCL/CRC-aided-SCL noiseless round-trips to (256,128), the SC ≥ SCL ≥ CA-SCL block-error ordering under AWGN, channel polarisation + capacity conservation, and CRC consistency). And now THE LOSSY PILLAR — a from-scratch, baseline (sequential-DCT, Huffman) JPEG codec that finally carries the lab past the entropy floor by discarding information ON PURPOSE, but only the information the eye cannot see: it realises Shannon's THIRD theorem, RATE–DISTORTION. Full pipeline, zero deps: BT.601 RGB↔YCbCr with 4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 chroma subsampling; an orthonormal separable 8×8 DCT-II (its inverse the exact transpose, so idct∘fdct is the identity to 1e-9); the Annex-K quantisation tables scaled by an IJG quality factor — the one lossy step, where most coefficients collapse to zero; the zig-zag scan; DC differential + category/magnitude coding and AC run/size coding with ZRL and end-of-block; the standard Annex-K Huffman code tables; and a byte-stuffed entropy stream wrapped in a real JFIF container (SOI/APP0/DQT/SOF0/DHT/SOS/EOI). The decoder mirrors it exactly — marker parse, canonical Huffman decode (min/max-code tables), dequantise, inverse DCT, and libjpeg-style FANCY (triangle-filter) chroma upsampling, with DRI/restart-marker support — so it reads not just our own files but the browser's. The showstopper, mirroring the gzip/PNG interop proofs but for a lossy format: the BROWSER'S OWN JPEG decoder renders our .jpg (agreeing with our decoder to 62+ dB and reproducing the original to 36–49 dB PSNR), and OUR decoder reads the browser's canvas-encoded .jpg to 50+ dB agreement — two independent codecs converging on the same picture. Its Rate–Distortion Studio makes the theorem operational: an original→decoded→amplified-error triptych, a live R–D curve (fidelity vs bits-per-pixel, every point a real encode+decode, saturating exactly as the theorem predicts), a click-to-inspect 8×8 block walk-through (luma pixels → DCT coefficients → quantisation table → the handful of surviving quantised coefficients → the inverse-DCT reconstruction), a DC-vs-AC bit budget, and the annotated JFIF marker table. Wired into the Self-test as its own group — the DCT round-trip and flat-block/Parseval identities, the colour-transform inverse, quality-monotone fidelity, near-lossless behaviour at quality 100, grayscale, MCU edge padding on odd dimensions, deterministic output and byte-stuffing correctness — bringing the in-browser suite to 698 checks, all green, plus 6 live native-JPEG interop cross-checks. And now THE THEORETICAL KEYSTONE — a RATE–DISTORTION & QUANTISATION pillar that stops merely REACHING for limits it already knows in closed form and instead COMPUTES them from scratch. At its heart is the BLAHUT–ARIMOTO algorithm (Arimoto/Blahut 1972), one alternating-minimisation engine run in two dual directions: forwards it finds the exact CAPACITY C = maxₚ I(X;Y) of an ARBITRARY discrete memoryless channel by multiplicatively reweighting the input law by each input's information divergence, and it CERTIFIES the answer with the classic sandwich I_L = Σp·Dₓ ≤ C ≤ maxₓ Dₓ = I_U — so the gap between an achievable lower bound and a genuine upper bound, not a fixed iteration count, is the stopping test; backwards it traces the exact RATE–DISTORTION FUNCTION R(D) = min I(X;X̂) subject to E[d]≤D of any source by sweeping the Lagrange slope from the lossless corner (R→H) to the free corner (R→0 at D_max). It rediscovers the SKEWED capacity-achieving input of the asymmetric Z-channel and the every-other-symbol code of Shannon's noisy typewriter (C=log₂(K/2)) with no hint, and its numerical R(D) lands byte-on-formula atop the textbook H(p)−H(D) for a Bernoulli source under Hamming distortion and ½·log₂(σ²/D) for a Gaussian under squared error. Then the CONSTRUCTIVE side that spends the bits R(D) only promises: LLOYD–MAX, the optimal fixed-rate SCALAR quantiser, designed by alternating the two necessary conditions (nearest-neighbour cells ⇄ centroid reconstruction levels) for Gaussian/Laplacian/Uniform sources — exactly the per-coefficient quantiser inside JPEG — reproducing the known optima (Gaussian N=2 → level √(2/π), MSE 1−2/π; a uniform source's 1/N² law), beating the naive uniform quantiser, and riding the famous 6.02 dB-per-bit high-rate slope a fixed gap below the R(D) bound; and LBG (Linde–Buzo–Gray), the VECTOR quantiser grown by codeword splitting + generalised Lloyd, whose cells tile the plane to recover the space-filling/shape gain a scalar quantiser leaves on the table — the very reason R(D) is only reachable in the large-block limit. Its lab page is a four-section studio: a live capacity solver with a transition-matrix heatmap, the capacity-achieving input distribution and the convergence bound-sandwich; the R(D) curve drawn against its closed form; the Lloyd–Max transfer staircase over the source density beside a fidelity-vs-rate race (Lloyd–Max vs uniform vs the R(D) bound, the 6 dB/bit slope visible); and the LBG codebook with Voronoi colouring and its monotone distortion descent; and a fifth section for the closed-form GAUSSIAN TWIN — WATER-FILLING — where the same pour-to-a-flat-level geometry solves both duals: FORWARD water-filling allocates a power budget across parallel Gaussian sub-channels to maximise capacity (starving the noisiest channels entirely), and REVERSE water-filling allocates a distortion budget across a Gaussian VECTOR source to minimise rate — which is the EXACT theory of transform-coding bit allocation, the reason JPEG spends its bits on the low-frequency DCT coefficients and drops the high ones — shown beside a curve where optimal variance-aware allocation beats a flat split. Twenty-five new self-tests (the closed-form capacities, the useless-channel C=0, the bound sandwich closing, R(D) matching both formulae and being convex & non-increasing, the Lloyd–Max known optima and 6 dB/bit slope, the LBG distortion nesting D₈≤D₄≤D₂ with centroid stationarity, and the forward/reverse water-filling reductions to their closed forms) lift the in-browser suite to 723 checks, all green — capacity, R(D) and the optimal quantiser, the three theorems this entire lab has been circling, finally computed from scratch. And now A WHOLE NEW MODALITY — AUDIO — and with it the last big idea the lab was missing, LINEAR PREDICTION. It starts with the substrate: CODES FOR THE INTEGERS, the toolbox that appears the moment a coder must emit a number whose range it can't bound in advance — the UNIVERSAL codes (unary, Elias γ/δ/ω, and Fibonacci/Zeckendorf, which end in '11' and resynchronise after a bit flip), asymptotically within a constant factor of optimal for any finite-entropy distribution and needing no parameter; and the PARAMETRIC codes (GOLOMB, the exact optimal prefix code for a geometric source, its multiply-free special case RICE = Golomb(2^k), and EXP-GOLOMB, the ue(v)/se(v) integer code of H.264/H.265) that hug the Shannon floor once you name the source's decay — with zig-zag signed folding, truncated binary, and both an exhaustive and a closed-form optimal-parameter finder, all wrapped in a lab page that shows one value in every code, the codeword table across values, the length-vs-value curves (unary linear, Elias logarithmic, Rice's flat k-bit floor) and the expected-bits-vs-entropy 'which code wins?' race. Then the codec those codes were built for: a from-scratch, spec-faithful FLAC — the ubiquitous lossless-audio format (and the same idea inside Apple Lossless, Shorten and WavPack). A sound sample is very nearly a linear combination of the ones just before it, so FLAC subtracts off that prediction and codes only the small, white-ish RESIDUAL — which, shaped like a two-sided geometric, is exactly what a Rice code spends the fewest bits on; that is why it crushes audio gzip cannot touch. The full pipeline, all integer and all exactly invertible: INTER-CHANNEL DECORRELATION (stereo recoded as mid/side or left/right-side, whichever is smaller this frame, because a song's two channels are nearly the same signal); per-block PREDICTOR SELECTION among CONSTANT, VERBATIM, the five FIXED polynomial predictors (the closed-form finite differences of order 0–4), and an LPC predictor whose coefficients come from LEVINSON–DURBIN on the Welch-windowed autocorrelation and are quantised to 15-bit integers with a shift by FLAC's error-feedback scheme; PARTITIONED RICE coding of the residual (the block split into 2^p partitions, each free to pick its own optimal Rice parameter — a transient and the silence after it want different k's — with an escape to raw bits for the incompressible stretches); and a REAL BITSTREAM — the fLaC marker, a STREAMINFO metadata block, and frames carrying the 14-bit sync code, a UTF-8-coded frame number, and per-frame CRC-8 (header) + CRC-16 (whole frame). Because every predictor is integer and its coefficients are transmitted, the decoder replays the identical arithmetic and reconstructs the samples BIT-FOR-BIT — the same 'a correct model is automatically a correct codec' invariant PPM and context mixing rely on, proved by round-tripping every signal shape × stereo mode × subframe type × block size plus a 60-case fuzz with zero mismatches. Its lab page opens the codec up on real audio (procedural tones, a chord, a chirp, a Karplus–Strong pluck, a source–filter vowel, a detuned stereo pad, white noise — plus any .wav you drop in): it PLAYS the audio through the browser's own WebAudio, races FLAC against raw PCM, WAV and gzip(PCM) (tones land at 14–18% of raw, white noise at ~100%, exactly as theory says), shows the original waveform beside the tiny residual with the best-Rice bits/sample falling from ~15 to ~3 as prediction whitens the signal, tables what predictor each frame chose, paints the per-partition Rice parameters, lists the quantised LPC coefficients, and carries a live bit-exact round-trip badge — while a companion WAV container lets the browser both play what we emit and load what you bring. The in-browser Self-test grows to 810 checks (adding the integer-code round-trips, the exhaustive best-Rice-parameter proof, and 77 FLAC/WAV round-trips across every signal, stereo mode, subframe type and block size), all green — audio, and the linear-prediction + Rice-coding core of every lossless-audio codec, now built from scratch alongside everything else. And now THE REAL bzip2 — not the earlier bzip-lite toy but the GENUINE .bz2 CONTAINER, byte-compatible with the Unix bzip2/bunzip2 tools: the lab had every Burrows–Wheeler part as an isolated primitive (BWT, move-to-front, RLE, package-merge Huffman, the bzip2 CRC) but no format that assembled them into a real, interoperable stream, and this is that format, implemented to the spec end to end. Per block: RLE1 (runs of ≥4 bytes → 4 literals + a count, bounding the sort's worst case); a full rotation BWT keeping bzip2's origPtr (a prefix-doubling suffix sort, differentially checked against the lab's reference BWT); move-to-front over the block's used-byte alphabet, which turns the BWT's clusters into a sea of zeros; RLE2's bijective RUNA/RUNB base-2 zero-run codes; and bzip2's signature MULTI-TABLE HUFFMAN entropy stage — 2–6 canonical Huffman tables (length-limited to 20 bits by the lab's own package-merge), refined over four passes so each 50-symbol group picks the cheapest table, its choices transmitted as MTF-coded selectors — a poor-man's context model for the price of one selector per group. It is wrapped in the exact bzip2 bit-stream: the BZh-level stream header, the π and √π block/footer magics, the sparse 16×16 symbol map, 24-bit origPtr, and — critically — bzip2's own NON-REFLECTED CRC-32 (MSB-first, poly 0x04C11DB7) per block plus the rotate-left-XOR combined stream CRC, so the checksums match bit-for-bit. The proof, mirroring the gzip/PNG/JPEG interop showcases: our from-scratch decoder reads real .bz2 files written by the Unix bzip2 tool (demonstrated live in the browser on an embedded real-tool stream), and our encoder's output is accepted and round-tripped by bunzip2 — validated in development across a 300-case fuzz (every content class × every bzip2 compression level) and multi-block streams, with zero mismatches. Its lab page opens the pipeline up stage by stage — the surviving-symbol counts through RLE1/BWT/MTF, the BWT last column with its manufactured runs, the MTF/RLE2 symbol stream coloured by RUNA/RUNB/value/EOB, the per-table code-length spans with the selector histogram, the sparse alphabet and the live block/stream CRCs — beside a one-click .bz2 download and the live interop badges. The in-browser Self-test grows to 855 checks (adding a differential BWT-vs-oracle proof and full .bz2 encode→decode round-trips with per-block CRC verification across the corpus and adversarial edge cases), all green — the canonical Burrows–Wheeler compressor, byte-compatible with the tool millions use, now built from scratch alongside everything else.
